Subject: Post-call: Dataflow, telemetry vendors & subprocessor approvals

Hi Samir / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery focused on data handling and third-party sharing. I tagged Marissa (CS) and Neha (Privacy) so we have direct coverage on operational and compliance items.

Summary of what we heard from Finlytics:
- You will send LLM requests containing PII (customer emails and hashed IDs) for enrichment and summarization.
- Required retention: request/response logs retained for up to 90 days for troubleshooting; redacted copies retained 12 months for analytics.
- Marketplace flow: some customers may provision via cloud marketplace; telemetry/usage events currently flow to a third-party analytics vendor.
- Compliance priorities: SOC 2, control over subprocessors, and ability to restrict log forwarding to cloud provider vs. external telemetry vendors.

Open items / requests from your side (per call):
1) Can Redwood provide a list of subprocessors (telemetry, metrics, crash reporting) and an explicit statement on whether we share request/response payloads with any telemetry vendor?
2) Details on retention controls and whether PII can be redacted or pseudonymized before logs land in metrics streams.
3) For marketplace-provisioned customers, how does telemetry flow differ and can Finlytics opt out?
4) Any required paperwork (DPA / subprocessors addendum) or SOC artifacts to speed procurement.

Attached: redwood-dataflow-matrix.pdf (high-level mapping of where request/response and logs might touch subprocessors), SOC2 snapshot.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll loop in Rishi (security) for a short technical Q&A where we can walk through telemetry pipelines and retention controls — propose Tue 4/6 10:00–10:30 PT.
- We’ll produce a concise subprocessor list and a one-page note on telemetry retention & redaction options by EOD Tue.
- If acceptable, we’ll prepare a DPA addendum template to be reviewed by your procurement.

If any of that is off, call it out and we’ll adjust.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — useful recap. A few clarifying questions before we lock the technical Q&A: 

1) Telemetry vendors: can you confirm whether request/response payloads ever get forwarded to third-party telemetry vendors (Amplitude, Datadog, Sentry, Mixpanel, etc.)? We specifically need to know if raw requests (or even partially redacted requests) are stored outside Redwood-managed infrastructure.

2) Redaction options: is there an automated pipeline you support to remove PII before logs are emitted? Or would that be an integration we need to implement on our side?

3) Marketplace customers: we use the Azure marketplace for account provisioning. If a customer signs via marketplace, will any telemetry be routed differently (e.g., to our Azure subscription logs or to Redwood’s telemetry vendor buckets)?

4) SOC and subprocessors: procurement needs an explicit list of subprocessors used for logging/telemetry, and evidence that we can restrict sharing on a per-customer basis. If you can provide a short CSV or one-pager, that will speed review.

Would like the subprocessor list and retention note by Tue EOD as you suggested. Also please include any default redaction knobs you support (tokens, headers, full payload hash-only modes).

Thanks — Priya

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dataflow, telemetry vendors & subprocessor approvals

Thanks Priya — great questions. Looping Rishi (Security) and Neha (Privacy) to provide the most accurate responses; see answers below and attached lightweight artifacts. I’ll keep this short and we can expand on Tue’s technical Q&A.

Short answers (high level):
- Do we forward request/response payloads to telemetry vendors? No. By default, Redwood does not forward raw request/response payloads to third-party telemetry vendors. Telemetry vendors receive aggregated metrics, sampling events, and anonymized operational logs. We do support opt-in debug logging (explicit customer consent), which can include more detailed traces; that flow is gated, auditable, and governed by the DPA/subprocessor agreement.

- Redaction / pseudonymization options: Redwood supports pre-ingest redaction via SDK hooks and a server-side pseudonymization layer. Options we can enable per-customer: full-payload hash-only mode (store hashes instead of raw text), header-only capture, or selective-field redaction (regex / key mapping). We’ll include configuration examples in the note.

- Marketplace-provisioned customers (Azure): For marketplace customers we support two models: 
  1) Hosted via Redwood-managed tenancy (default): telemetry follows our standard channels (no raw payload forwarding).
  2) Private deployment / VPC (recommended for regulated customers): telemetry and logs can be configured to flow only to the customer’s cloud project (Azure subscription) — Redwood won’t route telemetry to vendor buckets in that mode.

- Subprocessor list & procurement artifacts: attached is a brief CSV of subprocessors (telemetry vendors, cloud infra, observability) and a short DPA addendum template. We also attached a SOC2 control snapshot for your security team to review.

Attachments included in this message: redwood-dataflow-matrix.pdf, soc2-snapshot-2026.pdf, subprocessors-telemetry-list.csv (2 columns: vendor, purpose).

Proposed technical Q&A agenda (Tue 4/6 10:00 PT, 30 mins):
- Walk dataflow diagram (aditya, rishi) — 10 min
- Retention and redaction knobs (neha) — 10 min
- Marketplace flow differences & procurement checklist (marissa) — 10 min

If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short ticket for procurement to start the DPA signing.

Cheers,
